result:
I'd make other people's inner lives feel as real to everyone as their own does.

Everyone knows, as a fact, that the stranger on the bus has a whole life as vivid and central as theirs. Almost no one feels it, except in flashes. I think a huge share of the world's misery lives in that gap. Cruelty, indifference, and most of what happens in wars and comment sections depend on the other person being a bit abstract, more scenery than someone. It's hard to cheat, humiliate, or bomb a person whose reality you actually feel.

I considered more concrete answers, like ending disease or childhood poverty, and they're probably easier to defend. But I suspect many of those problems are downstream of this one. We already have the resources to fix a lot of them. What we lack is the sustained sense that the people affected are as real as we are.

The catch is that at full intensity it would be unbearable. No one could function while feeling eight billion lives at once. So I'd want it as a dial turned up a few notches, not a floodgate. Even a small shift would change a lot.

What would yours be?
